questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a business glossary deliberately leave out?
options: How a term is technically implemented — which column, table, or query calculates it
The name of the term itself
Who owns the term
Whether the term is approved or still a draft
questions.explain: The glossary says what a term means in business language; implementation detail (which column or query) belongs in the data dictionary, covered in Chapter 3.

questions.q: Which of these is a business glossary term, as distinct from a technical metadata entry, per this lesson's example?
options: dbo.Customer.IsActiveFlag
'Active Customer'
A BIT column with a computed default
A database index name
questions.explain: 'Active Customer' is the business concept with a plain-language definition; dbo.Customer.IsActiveFlag is the technical, structural implementation of that concept.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the most common mistake when starting a glossary?
options: Building it one table at a time, so it ends up restating the database schema
Writing definitions that are too short
Assigning too many owners to a single term
Including too many related terms in each entry
questions.explain: A good glossary is organized around business concepts, not database tables — a term built table-by-table ends up as a thin schema restatement instead of real business vocabulary.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how many tables or systems can a single glossary term like 'Customer Lifetime Value' map to?
options: Exactly one, always
Potentially several — it's still one glossary term with one agreed definition
Zero — glossary terms never map to any table
A fixed maximum of two
questions.explain: A business concept can be calculated from multiple tables across multiple systems while remaining exactly one glossary term with a single agreed definition.

questions.q: Which fields does this lesson say a minimal, usable glossary entry should include?
options: Term, definition, owner, status, and related terms
Only the term name, nothing else
A SQL query and a database connection string
A screenshot of the table the term relates to
questions.explain: These map directly onto the core metadata fields from Lesson 3, applied to a business concept rather than a technical object.
